utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard it from villagers in Zmajevo, I think, and places like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can you tell us where you heard about the Serb guard?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot recall now. I really cannot remember. Really. It's been quite a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Where did you hear about the Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We knew about the Red Berets. I mean, if you are asking me about where they were staying, well, I did not mention the Red Berets staying in this area.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could all other microphones please be switched off.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: In Osijek and Baranja, at the time while you were there, there were no Red Berets; is my understanding correct?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not under the name of the Red Berets. Now, I mean, if you are saying that Badza Stojicic and them are the same thing and why I said Badza's Men at some point and whatever, well.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can you explain it to us. Who are Badza's Men? Who is the Serbian guard? Do you make a distinction at all among all of these different groups?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Red Berets were units of the MUP. The Serbian guard was Arkan's Group, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What about the White Eagles?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vuk Draskovic. I mean, well, one of the groups, I mean -- but I think they operated under the SPO.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm going to tell you that none of that was correct, but I'm not going to ask you for any further comment. I'm now going to move on. Tell me, you mentioned Frenki's Men and you mentioned what Mate Tenjajic had told you. Did you hear about that somewhere else as well while you were there?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not hear about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So you were only told this by Tenjajic; correct?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the barracks commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Tell us, please, where did you have this conversation with Tenjajic when he told you about it?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In his office.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: When was this?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean what day or what date? I can't recall the date, but it was around 9.00 in the morning, after breakfast. I know because we met every morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So where was this barrack where this conversation took place?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on the approaches from Beli Manastir, from Bezdan towards Beli Manastir.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So what is the closest town?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Beli Manastir. This was in the town itself. The barrack is on the outskirts of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Tell us, please, where were you -- did --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, could you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: My question was: In what direction did this convoy take? In what direction did the column go?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the direction of the town of Beli Manastir.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Where were you while this column was passing?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Mate Tenjajic's office. I also had an office of my own sort of where I also slept and used as my office.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So while this column was moving past, you didn't even look out to see who or what was in the column?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Why didn't you even glance at who was in the column?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we were told that in the field we could only contact the army representatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Witness, I'm not asking you about contacts. I'm asking you about why you didn't even take a look at who was in the column. Wasn't that why you were sent there, to provide information about the situation as it was in Beli Manastir area?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't even take a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, were you not even interested in who these forces were, the paramilitary forces coming from Serbia to Beli Manastir, the area that you were charged with?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was interested and I was advised by Mate Tenjajic about who it was that was coming in about. And it was a war time situation. I had some bad experience in Beli Manastir at the time, and I was fed up with everything, and I just wanted to get out of there as soon as I could. I didn't even leave the barrack. I ate in the canteen there, and I remained on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you know when Bilje was liberated?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you know who liberated Bilje?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you know whether there was a local police force in Beli Manastir?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Who was at the head of this local police?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the changes were a daily occurrence. There were Serbian forces there. I remember that for a time there was a certain Boro Dobrokes; he was an older man, some 70 years or so old, that I and Pero Lazukic called and asked to take on the duty of municipal assembly president. We were occasionally informed about the situation in the field, and he was informed of them, but his information was so scarce that it was unreliable. There were daily changes. And I remember that there was a Zuco [phoen] person who was so glorified in the media, radio stations, that he was the best sharp-shooter, that he targeted victims from a silo or somewhere. There was even an instance where a man was killed 5 metres away from me.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, my question to you was: Was there a presence of the state security in Beli Manastir?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was only military security. Pero Lazukic was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Was there a Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Boro Dobrokes, he had a sort of Crisis Staff, and he was also the president of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Would you please explain to us, in your statement, 65 ter 5305, paragraph 72.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please do not show this in public.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You said: "I found a certain Boro Dobrokesa who used to work for the administration before the war, and I appointed him as a town administrator in Beli Manastir."

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, maybe it wasn't written down correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, please allow me to put my question first. My question is this: Who authorised you to appoint an administrator, a town administrator, in Beli Manastir? Under whose authority did you do that?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe it wasn't properly translated that this was a town administrator. He came to the barrack himself and said that he was in charge of the Crisis Staff. And Pero Lazukic and I then asked him to take over all the other functions because there was general chaos there. And he told us that there was a problem with some villagers on the border, and there were people coming in from Hungary, crossing over, because it was not secure. We charged him with taking care of that too.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you know who Stanko Ivanovic [as interpreted] was?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you know who Milomir Petkovic is?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I asked about Stanko "Trivanovic," whereas in the transcript it says Stanko "Ivanovic."

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you know who Radoslav Zirlarevic [phoen] is?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you know who Vranic was?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel kindly turn on and off his microphone himself because the interpreters cannot hear the beginning and the end of his question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stanislav Vranic was the last person I asked about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you heard the request of the interpreters? If you are assisted by switching on and off the microphone, then parts are lost. So it takes some concentration, but would you please try to do it yourself or to instruct your assistants accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I issued instructions to my assistant, but apparently he's not really complying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He has had a hard day today, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Witness, do you know which JNA unit took control over Baranja?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there were some forces in the barrack which took part in that, but which exact units they were, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Witness, do you know who General Krstic is?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't. Maybe it rings familiar, but I'm not -- I can't recall now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you know who Colonel Jovanovic was, the commander of the 36th Armoured Battalion?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: In your statement in paragraph 72, I think we still have it on our monitors.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: That's the previous page. If we can just switch pages. And let's -- it shouldn't be shown in public.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You say there: "My main task there was to go to the villages around Beli Manastir. I went to the villages and spoke with the people. The people complained that they were being attacked during the night, allegedly by Croats who were crossing in from Hungary." And so on and so forth. I never found anywhere in your statements that you said that you ever stated to the investigators that people complained about paramilitary forces, Serb paramilitary forces, the people that you had conversations with me, and now I would like to ask you why that is so? Why didn't you mention that when you gave this statement in 2006? But you did mention attacks against civilians. So it's obvious that that question was put to you. But you only mentioned the Croats from crossing over from Hungary. So I'm asking you now, Why did you nowhere ever mention Serbian forces?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, maybe the question wasn't specific about which forces this related to, but is it correct that around the villages near Knezivac there were attacks by Croats. But the villages towards Beli Manastir, towards Darda, Bilje, and Osijek, the complaints were different.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could you tell me why you did not mention attacks by Serb paramilitary forces against civilians in Baranja? Do you have an answer or don't you have an answer?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't have an answer why I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: I would just ask that at least we look at the next paragraph where there is mentioning of Serbian snipers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean paragraph 73?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But that's comment rather than ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Yes, it's a comment about how his prior statement is summarised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may just reply. Here mention is made of a specific incident, and we've heard about this incident today, so there's nothing -- there's nothing at issue here. So I'm asking about the attacks against the people, the civilians, who remained in villages, attacks by paramilitary forces. There's nothing about that in the statement. As for the other incident, he mentioned that ten minutes ago. If I may continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may continue, and the parties are invited not to give a lot of comment either in re-examination or -- you can ask a question about it or in argument you can point at any incompleteness of the portions of the evidence that you are pointing at. Now, I -- there's one issue, however, which appears here to be important, that is, that we are quoting from a document which is not in evidence. So, therefore, if there are any portions you want to point at, then perhaps we find a way to get that into evidence so that we are not without the assistance of the other portions of the statement. Please proceed, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I will consult with my colleague and then maybe we will come up with a joint proposal by the Defence teams as to how to treat this statement from 2004 by this witness. Your Honours, I will need to ask your leave to do something, and I would like to show you a document that we found overnight. I think it's an important document, but unfortunately we don't have a translation. And I would like to take advantage of this witness being present. This is document 2D62, 65 ter, with your leave. Although there is no translation, I would like to use this document. This is a document from the collection that may be familiar to the Trial Chamber from some other cases. The Republic of Croatia, the patriotic war documents, and according to what it says in this collection, this was a document found in the office of the president of Croatia. And there is a number under which it was registered. Unfortunately, there is no translation, but I would like to show this document to the witness. And then once it has been translated, we can tender the document or do as you order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any reason to believe that the witness is aware of this document. Because it may be a document, if relevant, which could be bar tabled or -- because it seems to be an official document. But if you first ask the witness whether he is aware of this document. And then if you want to read a certain portion to him, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please assist us and give the witness the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: This is a document drafted by the president for co-ordination of the parties of Yugoslav orientation, Dr. Vida Matic [phoen]; the president of the executive council of Slavonia and Western Srem for the municipality of Beli Manastir, Borivoje Zivanovic [phoen]; and the commander of the defence staff of Beli Manastir, Major Borivoje Dobrokes. The document was drafted on the 11th of September, 1991, in other words, when the witness was there, and it's entitled "Declaration of Capitulation of Croatia." Witness, that is copy of this document, the transcript of this document. This is not what it looked like in the original. My question to you is: Are you aware that these three individuals issued this type of declaration on the 11th of September, 1991?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see this declaration when I was there. I'm not familiar with it. But if you like, I can comment on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, I will put a question to you about what is stated under number 1. It says there, Baranja is free. The entire territory is under the control of the TO Beli Manastir units and MUP forces, or rather, SUP forces of the Beli Manastir municipality. In Baranja, the military rule was in place for three days only, after which a new executive government was elected in the autonomous region of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, the Executive Council for Baranja. Do you know whether what is stated here happened in Baranja immediately before this date as noted here, the 11th of September, 1991?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Would you please now take a look at paragraph 4. It says there: To the citizens of Baranja, you are invited to return. We guarantee freedom, law and order. Baranja is today under the control of JNA units and units of the territorial Defence, and there are no paramilitary units or organisations in our area. Is this consistent with what you knew about the situation there at the time when you were in Baranja?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Is it consistent with the statement that you gave in 2004 which is identical to what is stated in paragraph 4 here as it relates to military units in Baranja?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to Beli Manastir only or -- well in Baranja there were paramilitary units.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, could you assist us in telling us where we find a -- as you said, an identical statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can find that -- well, the 65 ter number is 5305. Paragraph 76. Not to be shown to the public, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll just read it into the record so that we know what we are talking about. It's a short paragraph. "I knew that the following paramilitaries were in the --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "I knew that the following paramilitaries were in the region of Eastern Slavonia. Those of Zeljko Raznjatovic, also known as Arkan, units commanded by Radovan Stojicic, also known as Badza," and then I leave out a -- something between brackets, for obvious reasons, "men of Vuk Draskovic and Vojislav Seselj. As far as I know, at the time, those paramilitaries had not been operating in Baranja because the area was under control of the JNA." So there we have that now on the record. Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would now like to ask that this document be marked for identification, the one that I showed just now. And then we will deal with it again when we have a translation that we can bring to the attention of the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll proceed as you suggest. It is a document under the number 152, dated the 11th of -- "Rujan" is what month again, Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, "Rujan" is September, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, 1991. And it is -- yes, I see it further down, 11/9/1991, and it is a declaration or a statement given by the persons you mentioned. Madam Registrar, the number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit D58, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. And we wait for it to be uploaded and a translation to be provided. Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, in your earlier statement you said that the JNA had had an important role in setting the borders of the SAO Krajina. Tell us how.

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When there was a conflict between certain villages, the villagers would place roadblocks in order to protect themselves. Then on the following day we would go there to see the localities involved, Vratisti [phoen], Vratiskovac [phoen], its characteristic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: My question was one that required only a brief answer. I think I'm getting to the very end. In this statement, 5305, 65 ter, in paragraph 39, you said that the JNA was not involved in the separation of forces, rather, they -- is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel kindly repeat the last part of his sentence, please, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Two questions now. Three, actually, if you allow me. Mate Tenjic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Limited time, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just three questions and I'm done.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So, Mate - I want to get the last name right - Mate Tenjajic, can you tell us what his ethnicity was?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Was anybody else present when you and Tenjajic talked, and is he alive today, and where can we find him, if you know?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I think Pero Lazukic was there too, and I heard that Pero got killed. I know that his wife came to Belgrade, but I really don't know about Mate Tenjajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Last question: Did you write report during your stay in Kninska Krajina and in Slavonia, or rather, Baranja?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Kninska Krajina, yes; in Osijek, yes; in Baranja, I just wrote daily notes in my notebook. I wrote things in my notebook earlier on as well and then based my notes on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you ever convey the information that you received to anyone while you were in Baranja?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to Petar Gracanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you write that up when you came to Belgrade? Did you write up a report?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, on behalf of both Defence teams, I would like to ask that the previous statements of this witness that is marked as 5305 on the 65 ter list be admitted into evidence because we put many questions on the basis of that statement, and I believe that it can be of great assistance to the Trial Chamber when assessing the evidence given by this witness. Of course, I'm tendering it under seal. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It may create quite a bit of problems to deal with it in this way because the only way of having it admitted would be under Rule 92 ter. Now, there's as such no problem to that, but then we should give the witness an opportunity to first read it all and then to make the relevant attestations. And that's exactly the reason why I said that we have to find a way of getting into evidence - and that's the reason why I read even literally one paragraph - in order to have the relevant context. We'll consider it. But even not knowing the response of the Prosecution, the Chamber might be quite hesitant to follow this alternative route without the witness having had an opportunity to review his statement. And, nevertheless, he would have to give the attestations. That's really problematic, Mr. Petrovic, from a procedural point of view.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I fully understand that, Your Honour. So although I haven't consulted my colleague from the Stanisic Defence, I think that we could approach this in an alternative fashion, namely, the parts of his statement that were read out before the Honourable Trial Chamber and that the parties dealt with, could those parts be admitted into evidence and the rest can be simply ignored.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Whether we can admitted it into evidence or whether the parties could agree that that is what the witness stated at the time and then select the paragraphs, then we have a -- at least a context. Now, let's first see. Any need for re-examination, Mr. Hoffmann?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Yes, very briefly. If I may just add one sentence to the issue of the tendering of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: I think the relevant parts have been read into the transcript when there was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can check that. And apparently what we want is that if reference was made to the earlier statements when questions were asked that in one way or another that it's put on the record what is in that earlier statement relevant for the questions and for understanding the answers. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, very briefly a number of questions. Today you were asked in the context of the take-over of the federal MUP building, and that is today at transcript page 17, there was a suggestion made to you that documents were taken away by thieves and not just by colleagues or other services. If you mentioned documents missing in the federal DB or the federal MUP, did you have in mind general criminals coming into the federal MUP and taking away documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry to leap up. I wasn't - just so that we are clear so the issue can be expedited - I wasn't suggesting, if I can put it this way, common criminals. I was suggesting employees taking documents, thereby becoming thieves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I remember -- I was about, when you put the question the way in which you phrased it, to ask whether this was really what you meant. Because theft being more, I think, more vulnerable for thieves, I think you said, that, of course, was the suggestion. But let's -- Mr. Hoffmann, I take it that we are not discussing here whether ordinary thieves would, in order to get some paper, in order to -- for whatever reason -- the matter seemed to be clear the suggestion was not ordinary thieves. Apart from that, the witness did not respond to that suggestion. He said papers disappeared. That's the evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: I'm just looking at the record, Your Honours, and I'm sorry to repeat, but at transcript 7 [sic] it says, you know: "... the federal MUP ... became vulnerable to thieves and state confidential material started to disappear, is that fair?" And he said in the answer: "It was to start earlier ..." So at least if we now agree that it wasn't meant to be that thieves would come and pick up documents, then I can leave it there. But the record is pretty clear that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Paper disappeared. And it is not suggested and since we do not have evidence at this moment on who had stolen that, that there's no reason to assume at this moment that these were ordinary thieves coming from the street. Is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That's correct. And the evidence was given --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- I consider that it really doesn't assist the Chamber to explore in full depth this issue. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Yes, I move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, during your testimony yesterday -- no, let me start this way. Today you were asked a number of questions about the presence and what you learned about Frenki's Men. Now, I just want to recall what you stated yesterday on the record, and that is at transcript T4847. You stated, and I quote: "Since I was tasked by my superior as the leader of the group for Osijek to try and verify the situation in Srem and Osijek, I went together ..." and I'll cut it short "... together we visited some of the villages near Manastir and in the town itself." And later on you said you talked to people in the villages, and I quote then: "They also talked about the presence of Chetniks, Chetnik detachments, about Badza's Group or groups, also about the presence of Frenki's Men, the Red Berets, Badza's Group ..." And so on. Now, my question to you is: Apart from what you stated during cross today that from a particular person in the barracks in Beli Manastir, did you also learn from those villagers about the Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that from the villagers because they were mostly elderly people. They said Chetniks, paramilitaries, Arkan's Men, White Eagles. I have no idea. I mean, please don't take my word for it now for each and every one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Okay. I'll leave it at that. I want to bring up a just a video still, and that is of the so-called Kula camp video. Exhibit P61. And we are looking at minute 4, 43 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Before the -- I beg your pardon. If my learned friend is attempting to elicit new evidence concerning the identification of one of the men mentioned during the witness's testimony present or allegedly present at the Kula award ceremony, then we object. This should have been dealt with in chief. It is opening a new line of examination --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann, where does it arise from the cross-examination the question that you would like to put to the witness at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: I'm having difficulties to directly respond without, with my explanation, lead the witness of the possible identification on those witnesses. But it is about a key person that we've talked about yesterday and today that he has knowledge of. I'm not going to ask anything else than to identify the person. And I've tried to talk to both Defence teams even during the break, whether we could just agree whether that particular person did attend, yes or no. I understand that both weren't sure about it and that's why they couldn't agree. So all I want to establish --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any dispute as to the identity of that person on this picture? I mean ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We don't know. We spoke to Mr. Hoffmann before the break and we said we weren't in a position to confirm or deny and we wanted time to consider it. And we thought that was the end of the matter with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as opposed to our friend Mr. Jordash we lived there at the time and we can say what the identity of that first person here is, that is to say, we can confirm what he wanted to get from the witness. But what would that amount to? Our testimony here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, a matter that you agree upon with the Prosecution, that the person to the left on this is -- do you agree on who it is? Who is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, so if the question is just, Who is this person in front of us, we can agree on that. However, we cannot say where the picture was taken, how, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Fine. Who is it as far as you are concerned?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Petar Gracanin. The first man on the left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In agreement with the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's on the record. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Last question, witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I do apologise. May this part where it says where it is from, everything that is to be said is who the person is. That can be put to the witness, nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you agree. Now, Mr. Jordash, are you going to challenge that, or would you join in the agreement? Perhaps if you want to take instructions, then ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We join in the agreement. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. All three parties agree that it's Mr. Gracanin. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And very briefly, Witness, you were asked today whether you had expected any assistance from the Tribunal when giving evidence and obviously the suggestion to you was that you fabricated your evidence. My question to you is: Did you ever invent any of your evidence before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't invent anything. Perhaps it's only the passage of time that affected my memory of persons, events, and situations. Otherwise I stand by everything I had said.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And my last question: Is it correct, Witness, that your request for asylum in the country that you reside in has actually been denied a number of years ago already?

utterances.speaker: JF-038 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has the re-examination triggered any need for further questions? Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
